rules.statement: When a GitHub CLI command is replaced by its REST API form, carry over the ordering the caller relies on, e.g. pass `sort=updated` and `order=desc` to `search/issues` when the most recently updated items are expected.
rules.why: Without explicit sort parameters GitHub's search returns best-match order, so a limited result set is no longer the most recently updated items the caller promises.
rules.check: Look for `gh api` calls to `search/issues` or other list endpoints that replace a `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` call; check they pass the sort/order parameters the consuming step assumes.

rules.statement: A call to a paginated REST list endpoint that reads only one page must either loop over pages or carry a comment next to it stating the cap and why it is enough.
rules.why: Otherwise results beyond the first page are dropped silently, and a reader can't tell whether the truncation was intended.
rules.check: Find list calls with `per_page=` and no page loop; flag them when no adjacent comment names the cap and justifies it.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a page loop or a test of paging on a single-page list call whose comment states the cap and why the filtered result stays below it.
rules.why: The maintainer accepts a documented cap that matches the previous limit when the filter keeps results far below it; a loop and test would add nothing.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing page loop, read the comment above the call; if it states the cap and the justification, don't report it.

rules.statement: Give each fallback path for a failed external read (non-zero exit, unparsable response, non-404 error) a test that forces the failure and asserts the fallback value.
rules.why: Without one, a regression could misreport state or throw, or make a failed read look like an empty result, and no check would fail.
rules.check: For new or changed failure branches around API or CLI reads, look for a test case that makes the read fail and asserts the resulting state.

rules.statement: Test escaping or encoding logic with input that contains characters the escaping actually changes, and assert the encoded value.
rules.why: Input that needs no escaping lets a regression that drops the escaping pass unnoticed.
rules.check: Look at tests of URL or data escaping; flag them when every input is unchanged by the escape function, e.g. a branch name with no `/`.

rules.statement: Don't report that a cross-reference in a template points to the wrong section until you've checked where its included partials expand in the generated output.
rules.why: Included partials can place content inside the referenced section of the generated copies even though it isn't in the template source.
rules.check: Trace the include directives, e.g. `{{PROMPT:...}}`, in the referenced section and look at the generated copy before reporting a cross-reference as wrong.
